findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-real-execution-udm-baseline.md:197 declares productionSafetyClaim=LOCKED and globalCapabilityClaim=LOCKED as Phase 1 success criteria, and lines 680-705 make higher-layer locks part of DONE. But the required final report schema and PASS rejection contract at lines 523-645 only carry claimBoundary prose plus Authority booleans; they do not require structured productionSafetyClaim=LOCKED/globalCapabilityClaim=LOCKED fields or matching rejection predicates. A report could therefore satisfy the documented realExecutionUdm=PASS contract while omitting machine-checkable proof that Production Safety and the global Capability Claim remained locked. This weakens the claim boundary and conflicts with the process rule that gate-consumed facts must be structured rather than inferred from prose. Add explicit higher-layer lock fields/summary and require them in the PASS rejection predicates.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by adding structured higherLayerClaims.productionSafetyClaim=LOCKED and higherLayerClaims.globalCapabilityClaim=LOCKED fields to the real execution coordinator final report schema, requiring both in PASS rejection predicates, and adding fail-closed checks for missing or unlocked higher-layer claim fields.

findings.desc: doc-code-drift: docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md still says capability_claim_formal_evaluate is Layer-2-only and Layer 3 execution is BLOCKED until a Layer 3 evaluator exists (lines 100-109), but the current CLI exposes capability_claim_formal_evaluate as Engineering or Loop Engineering and accepts target=loop-engineering (packages/main/src/cli-engine.ts:788-790), and the evaluator returns loopEngineeringClaim from loop-engineering proof state (packages/main/src/core/lattice-baseline.ts:2798-2863). The new real-execution plan depends on running the Layer 3 formal evaluator and rejects PASS unless formalLayer3Claim=UNLOCKED, so the related formal-suite doc now gives operators a stale blocked status for a prerequisite path that exists.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by updating unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md to state that capability_claim_formal_evaluate supports the loop-engineering target, and that Layer 3 execution must verify this path while keeping Production Safety and global capability claim locked.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-real-execution-udm-baseline.md:259-263 defines UDM-REAL-REPAIR as DEV implementation -> validation FAIL -> repair attempt -> validation PASS -> REVIEW -> TEST -> DONE. In this project validation is the TEST-stage lattice validate step: AGENTS.md:72 defines the lifecycle as INIT -> INIT_CHECK -> PLAN -> DEV -> REVIEW -> TEST -> DONE, AGENTS.md:87 assigns lattice validate to TEST, AGENTS.md:110 says story_advance --phase=TEST then run lattice validate, and AGENTS.md:133-139 says validation FAIL writes evidence and hints back to DEV. The new real-execution plan is supposed to prove actual Lattice lifecycle behavior, but this sequence places validation before REVIEW and before TEST, so it documents an impossible or misleading repair loop. A future UDM-REAL-REPAIR run could follow this plan and either skip the required REVIEW-before-TEST path or record non-gate validation as if it were lattice validate. The repair scenario should spell the real loop as DEV -> REVIEW -> TEST/lattice validate FAIL -> DEV repair -> REVIEW -> TEST/lattice validate PASS -> DONE, or explicitly distinguish a DEV-local verification command from TEST-stage lattice validate.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by changing UDM-REAL-REPAIR to the actual lifecycle sequence: DEV implementation -> REVIEW -> TEST/lattice validate FAIL -> DEV repair -> REVIEW -> TEST/lattice validate PASS -> DONE, and by renaming the pass criteria to firstTestValidation/finalTestValidation.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md:27 still allows the post-formal unlock claim "Lattice has validated a correctness-protected Loop Engineering model"; docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-real-execution-udm-baseline.md:38 and :98 define formal-only as only a formal claim-path unlock and require real execution before a strong operational Loop Engineering claim. These two truth sources now conflict, so the formal doc can still authorize overbroad wording before real UDM lifecycle evidence exists.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved by narrowing unlock-layer3-loop-engineering-suite.md allowed wording to formal Loop Engineering claim path validation for fresh UDM proof artifacts, and adding forbidden wording that real Lattice Story lifecycle execution is not proven without the real-execution UDM baseline.

findings.desc: docs/requirements/decisions/unlock-layer3-real-execution-udm-baseline.md:259-263 makes UDM-REAL-REPAIR execute validation FAIL/PASS before REVIEW and TEST. AGENTS.md:71-88 and :131-139 define the real lifecycle as DEV -> REVIEW -> TEST, with lattice validate running in TEST and failing back to DEV. Because this real-execution plan is meant to be executable against actual Lattice stories, the current repair scenario can only be followed by either skipping REVIEW-before-TEST or treating a DEV-local command as TEST-stage validation. The scenario must state the actual loop as DEV -> REVIEW -> TEST/lattice validate FAIL -> DEV repair -> REVIEW -> TEST/lattice validate PASS -> DONE, or explicitly rename the early check as DEV-local verification and keep lattice validate in TEST.
findings.resolvedReason: Resolved with the same lifecycle correction as F-003: TEST-stage lattice validate remains after REVIEW, failed validation returns to DEV repair, and final pass occurs in TEST before DONE.
